text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam and Thailand have signed an agreement on sea borders in the Gulf of Thailand.

-- The National Assembly's Standing Committee says a revised law for the National Assembly and the election of the highest state offices will be among the first tasks for the legislature's coming session.
-- Vice-President of the State Securities Commission, Nguyen Duc Quang, says plans for a Stock Exchange have been submitted to the government.
-- About 70,000-100,000 people migrate to Ho Chi Minh City every year. Most are not eligible for permanent residence.
-- Agriculture and Rural Development Minister Nguyen Cong Tan says farmers should not mortgage their property when taking out bank loans.
-- Vietnam expects to produce 10 million tonnes of coal in 1997.
-- The southern province of Dong Thap harvested 130,000 hectares of paddy ahead of floods there.
-- More than 2.1 million of tonnes of rice have been exported, and 301,000 tonnes sold on the domestic market so far this year.
-- The government says its target during the remaining months of 1997 will be to deal with stagnation in the production, business and investment environments.
